dedupe_keys.name: bp fatar public tree and park cadastre application of budapest fokert

description: BP Fatár is the public tree and park cadastre application of Budapest, developed by the municipal gardening company FŐKERT with the support of the capital and launched in 2020 as the public version of the green asset inventory that Hungarian law requires municipalities to keep. The page read on 2026-09-28 says the application has three main sections, the tree cadastre, the park cadastre and locally protected areas, with more than 300 hectares of city forests added in January 2022; at launch it covered about 47,000 park trees and 30,000 street trees owned by the capital, all parks it maintains, all local nature protection and forest areas, and 155 notable trees with a computed tree value and short history, and districts XIII, I, VI and XIV have since joined, with a fault reporting function for citizens. Coverage is Budapest's municipal green areas. Access is free in the application; no licence or data export is stated. Caveats: district-owned trees appear only for districts that joined. It supports storm and heat exposure studies, such as tree fall risk to streets, tramlines and overhead lines. Related record: data-bratislava-stare-mesto-tree-map-gisplan is a comparable city tree map.
